newsitem.title: JAPAN: NTT sweetens early retirment plan to cut staff.
newsitem.headline: NTT sweetens early retirment plan to cut staff.

text.p: Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp (NTT) President Junichiro Miyazu said on Wednesday that the company plans to sweeten its early retirement programme in the current fiscal year, ending next March, in order to speed up staff reduction.

Miyazu declined to comment on whether NTT has any plans to revise downward its target parent company work force of 150,000 by 2000, compared with 182,500 as of end-March 1997, although he added, "It would be desirable if the work force were cut below 150,000 by the year 2000."
Under NTT's new early retirement programme, the company will increase its one-time cash payment to employees opting for the scheme by the equivalent of an extra 12-months' pay, Miyazu said.
He added that NTT also expanded the age range of workers eligible for the programme to 40-57, from 45-55.
Miyazu said NTT had no target for the number of people expected to opt for the early retirement scheme.
